title: Occupancy-prediction-led writeback and sparse-rescue protocol for paged KV
creator: Sofia Ortega
description:
Problem: Paged KV caches are experiencing high tail latency and repeated churn when small-interleaved requests cause frequent partial writes and reactive eviction storms. Current eviction heuristics (LRU variants + size tiers) create oscillation across hot and warm fragments; kernels are suboptimally selected because prefill hints are noisy at admission time.

Proposal: Introduce an occupancy prediction layer that estimates short-horizon residency for incoming token spans and uses that signal to: (1) delay writeback for low-utility fragments and batch them into opportunistic restore windows, (2) mark candidate fragments for "sparse-rescue" (cheap restore of high-reuse fragments), and (3) emit kernel-selection hints to the runtime to prefer compact, low-memory kernels for fragments predicted to be short-lived and high-throughput kernels for predicted long-residency fragments.

Key ideas: occupancy predictor (lightweight time-decay model + tenant-weighted features), writeback batching windows aligned to decode microbatches, rescue sampler that opportunistically rehydrates evicted fragments when low-cost kernel slots are available, and eviction-smoothing (soft quotas with decaying credits) to avoid oscillation. Coordination with prefill/decode scheduler: predictor output should be consulted at prefill admission and decode start to decide whether to prefill, defer, or route to a compatible kernel variant with different memory/perf tradeoffs.

Why unique: Combines a predictive admission signal with policy-driven writeback and a low-cost rescue path, focusing on reducing tail decode latency and cross-tenant thrashing rather than purely maximizing hit-rate. Includes explicit kernel-hinting to help the runtime choose quantized/compact kernels earlier, reducing overhead for ephemeral fragments.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end benchmark: 99th percentile decode latency reduced by >= 20% on mixed short/long sequence workload compared to baseline (current LRU-based eviction)
Total token throughput remains within 5% of baseline under steady-state load
KV churn (evictions per minute) reduced by >= 30% for multi-tenant interleaved workload trace
Kernel selection correctness: at least 85% of kernel-hints issued by predictor match the kernel chosen by the runtime after final profiling checks
Feature gated behind runtime flag 'occupancy_rescue_v1' with telemetry for predictor confidence, deferred-writeback counts, and rescue success rate
Unit and integration tests covering predictor on synthetic traces, writeback batching, and rescue admission logic
Conservative rollout plan: 10% of traffic -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback on key SLO regressions
comments: 2026-02-10 Sofia Ortega: Triage notes - observed repeated eviction/restores in production trace from advertising customer. Decided to explore predictive admission instead of tuning LRU windows.

2026-02-18 Liam Chen: Proto-sim completed. Synthetic trace (mix of 8-64 token spans) shows 25% reduction in evictions using time-decay predictor with tenant weighting. Need to refine writeback window heuristic to avoid increasing average latency.

2026-02-22 Priya Menon (PM): Design review feedback - ensure rescue path respects tenant isolation and does not prioritize cross-tenant warmup that could violate fairness. Add soft quotas per-tenant for rescue budget.
2026-02-24 Anya Patel (Security): Quick note - rescue metadata contains only fragment fingerprints and occupancy estimates, no PII. KMS access unaffected. No major security blockers.

2026-02-26 Engineering sync: Decided on predictor feature set: last-touch decay, reuse-frequency counter, inbound-request-size histogram. Will emit a three-tier hint: DEFER, PREFILL_LIGHT, PREFILL_HEAVY. Kernel hint map added: DEFER->none, PREFILL_LIGHT->compact kernel, PREFILL_HEAVY->fast kernel.

2026-03-01 Liam Chen: Integrated kernel-hint propagation into prefill admission path. Running clustered A/B on replay for 48h. Early telemetry: deferred-writeback up 12%, rescue-success 43%. Collecting more samples to confirm tail latency benefits. Next: add eviction-smoothing credits and tenant budget enforcement.
